headline: A Nigerian researcher has won a $100,000 national science prize for AI software she says can cut MRI scan times by up to 90%.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a national prize and big speed claims, but the figures are the inventor's own and the tool is not yet in clinical use.
importance_line: If the claim holds, hospitals could scan more patients on the MRI machines they already have and shorten diagnosis queues, but the figures come from the inventor, the tool has yet to go through regulatory submission and clinical trials, and commercial use is not expected before the second half of 2027.
summary: The Sun Nigeria reports that Mary-Brenda Akoda, a Nigerian AI researcher, won the $100,000 Nigeria Prize for Science and Innovation, organized by Nigeria LNG Limited (NLNG), for GenScan AI, software she says rebuilds diagnostic-quality MRI images from far less scan data and so can cut scan times by up to 90%. The performance figures are Akoda's own: she says a blinded check by one consultant radiologist at a UK NHS hospital judged the images diagnostically equivalent in the cases assessed, while regulatory submission and clinical trials are still to come and she is targeting commercial use in the second half of 2027.
notes: Full text read from fulltext/C10-10.txt (The Sun Nigeria's own reporting). Other Nigerian outlets also carry the prize; performance figures are the inventor's claims.
